long_biography.plain_text:
Selling Pacific & Atlantic's dry-cargo fleet before the global financial crisis defined Nikolas D. Pateras's first major shipping cycle. The company had operated more than 100 bulk and multipurpose vessels, but the disposal left him outside shipowning as the market turned sharply down.

Pateras re-entered through a different niche in 2015, founding Contships Management around second-hand feeder containerships. Beginning with three vessels, he built a homogeneous fleet serving major charterers and retained direct control as chairman, chief executive and majority owner. The company later won the Lloyd's List Greek Shipping Award for Dry Cargo Company of the Year.

uncertainties.detail: The source record uses Nikos Pateras; first-party and regulatory materials use Nikolas D. Pateras, while Forbes Greece uses Nikolaos Pateras. The exact Contships, Pacific & Atlantic and Pateras Brothers sequence establishes these as forms of the same person's name. Other Pateras shipowners, including George Pateras and members of separate family branches, were excluded.

Pateras took over management of an established family company and 11-vessel fleet, then established and substantially expanded Pacific & Atlantic before founding Contships. Public material does not disclose whether the initial fleet was inherited, gifted, jointly owned or merely placed under his management, so Mixed is used instead of asserting a pure legal inheritance or a purely self-made start.

Forbes Greece and To Vima identify Athens as Pateras's birthplace. His family originates from Oinousses, which an existing reference site's infobox inconsistently labels as the birthplace even though its prose says Athens. Athens is proposed at high, not very-high, confidence.

No identity-secure personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X or personal website was located. Search results were company pages, third-party posts or namesakes. The existing Wikipedia profile is retained and the official Contships site is proposed only as a Company Website.

Forbes Greece includes Pateras in a shipowners feature, but no dedicated profile exists on Forbes' personal-profile path. The dossier therefore records not_found rather than treating the list article as a verified Forbes profile.

Sports and political controversies, allegations, legal matters, private-family trivia, vessel-specific research and transient net-worth estimates are excluded. His family shipping background is retained only because it materially explains the platform from which his own businesses developed.
